experiment: AUTH-03 identity rules: does the shape alone raise a candidate, and if not which precondition is missing
question: ability_ability_runtime @ 4ae23f04b8f4, services/abilitymgr/src/ability_manager_stub.cpp:3464-3467 reads a permission name, a pid and a uid out of the parcel and hands them to VerifyPermission, yet no ipc.auth.request-identity candidate came out of the component. Is the rule unable to see request-derived identity, or is a precondition unmet?
method: The detector runs twice per case, once with the base pass and once with complete-ast, on unit tuples built in memory. Cases 1-7 combine the fixture declarations in tests/fixtures/ipc/common_types.h with statement text; cases 8-9 feed the real component's own files. Nothing is written to the corpus.

cases.what: the four real statements verbatim inside an entry, followed only by reply.WriteInt32
the same four statements plus StartAbility() on the same path
request-derived value handed to the same predicate, with the effect
the caller's own TokenID handed to the same predicate, with the effect
GetSelfTokenID() handed to VerifyAccessToken, with the effect
GetCallingUid() handed to VerifyAccessToken, with the effect
a same-file helper named VerifyPermissionInner, body = the real statements plus a sensitive effect, called by name from the entry

results: The rule can see request-derived identity: cases 2, 3 and 7 raise ipc.auth.request-identity, at the line of the predicate call, with a non-zero line number.

The shape alone is not enough. The identical statements with nothing modelled after them (case 1) raise nothing at all -- the predicate is collected into state.identity_issues and only emitted when a call in sensitive_calls is reached on that path (analysis.py action()).
A helper whose name ends in Inner is not a barrier when it is in the same file and called by name (case 7). So the real component's silence is not explained by the handler's name.

The real file is parsed complete on both sides and still raises nothing for request-identity, although the shape is at :3465. Its caller is the IDL-generated dispatcher, which is not in the source tree, so the body is not on a path from any entry root: the same coverage gap as ipc.auth.caller-class, plus the missing sensitive effect.
Both-side control: the caller-token form (case 4) is silent while the request form (case 2) fires, so the rule is not simply flagging every predicate call.
scope_limits: Static re-run only. No build, no PoC, no dynamic validation.

Cases 1-7 are built from statement text and fixture declarations, not from the component's real translation unit; they establish which precondition the rule requires, not what the component's behaviour is.
The single request-derived site found by the text census is the permission check itself; nothing here says the component is vulnerable, and VerifyPermission's semantics are not established.

The argument census resolves one local-assignment hop. A value travelling through a container, a member or a function is counted as unresolved, so 0 caller_uid is a statement about this method, not a proof of absence.
